knobs.label: t3 average CPU (surplus credits above baseline)
knobs.why: t3 Unlimited bills $0.05 per vCPU-hour above the 40% baseline (t3.xlarge flat-out = $0.2864/h vs $0.1664 list).

knobs.label: t3 Unlimited: average CPU above baseline (share of each vCPU)
knobs.why: T3 Unlimited bills surplus CPU credits at $0.05/vCPU-h (Linux) when the 24 h average exceeds the baseline (30% t3.large, 40% t3.xlarge/2xlarge). t3 on-demand is $0.0416/vCPU-h, so each +10 points above baseline adds ~12% (factor = 1 + 1.202 x excess). Source: aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand (T2/T3/T4g Unlimited Mode Pricing) and the EC2 burstable credit table.

caveats: On-demand and RI rates: AWS Price List API (AmazonEC2 index.csv, version 20260925174521) for us-east-1, eu-north-1, ap-south-1 (also checked eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1 for xlarge). "Cheapest EU/Asia" means cheapest among regions checked.
Spot prices are a point-in-time snapshot of AWS's own spot feed and vary by AZ and hour. Savings Plan rates from AWSComputeSavingsPlan (2026-09-25).
Reserved/SP modes are modelled only for us-east-1; regional RI rates (e.g. eu-north-1 c7i.xlarge 1y $0.12641, ap-south-1 Graviton 1y $0.065) are in the regime write-up.
Windows licence-included = +$0.046/vCPU-h on c7i/m7i (on-demand and RI); t3 Windows is +$0.0184/vCPU-h; Graviton cannot run Windows; spot Windows spreads differ (c7i.xlarge spot Windows $0.2546).
Billing: per second with 60 s minimum (Linux, Windows). Stopped instances bill EBS and any public IPv4 but not compute.
EBS gp3 $0.08/GB-month us-east-1 (eu-north-1 $0.0836, ap-south-1 $0.0912) incl. 3,000 IOPS/125 MB/s; snapshots $0.05/GB-month (eu-north-1 $0.0475). No free root disk: add ~8-80 GB gp3.
Public IPv4: $0.005/h per address, in-use or idle (AmazonVPC price list, all regions checked) = $3.65/month at 730 h. Billed per ENI/instance that has a public IP.

NAT gateway gotcha: tasks/functions in private subnets reach the internet through a NAT gateway at $0.045/h per gateway (~$32.85/month per AZ) plus $0.045/GB processed (us-east-1; eu-north-1 $0.046, ap-south-1 $0.056), charged ON TOP of the $0.09/GB egress. Not modelled; public IPv4 ($0.005/h) is the usual alternative.

Internet egress (AWS Price List API, AWSDataTransfer us-east-1, 2026-09): first 100 GB/month free aggregated across all services and regions, then $0.09/GB first 10 TB, $0.085 next 40 TB, $0.07 next 100 TB, $0.05 over 150 TB. eu-west-1 is also $0.09; ap-south-1 $0.1093; ap-northeast-1 $0.114; ap-southeast-1 $0.12 (first-10-TB tier). The engine uses the flat us-east-1 first tier.
Boot takes tens of seconds; not a fast sandbox. AWS Free Tier $200 credit for new accounts is generic.

GPU modes cover single-GPU instances only (g6, g5, g6e, p5.4xlarge); 4x/8x bundles (H200/B200/B300, multi-L4/L40S) and fractional g6f slices are not modelled. Egress is priced at the first tier ($0.09/GB); AWS tiers are $0.09/$0.085/$0.07/$0.05 at 10/50/150 TB.

t3 Unlimited surplus credits ($0.05/vCPU-h Linux above the 24 h average baseline) are not charged unless you set the t3 surplus knob; the default assumes average CPU at or below baseline. burstable-t3 is flagged burstable (40% baseline) so sustained-load workloads see it as a compromise.
Reserved/Savings Plan regimes are flagged commit (1-year / 3-year); the RI is billed for every hour of the term whether or not the instance runs.
Boot overhead not encoded (no measured cold start in research/benchmarks.json): EC2 instances take tens of seconds to boot and are billed from the running state (60 s minimum).

Launch rate limits: RunInstances request bucket 5 (burst) refilled at 2/s, and a resource bucket of 1,000 instances refilled at 2 instances/s (StartInstances the same). A 1,000-instance burst is fine, after that ~7,200 launches/hour sustained; adjustable via Service Quotas.

New accounts: Running On-Demand Standard (A,C,D,H,I,M,R,T,Z) quota default = 5 vCPUs per region (Spot Standard also 5; G/VT and P = 0). That is ONE 4-vCPU instance at a time until EC2 auto-raises the quota with usage or a Service Quotas request is approved; stopped instances don't count.

Free plan (accounts created on/after 2025-07-15): $100 sign-up credit + up to $100 from activities, all expiring 12 months after sign-up. The Free plan (vs Paid plan) lasts 6 months or until credits run out, cannot overspend, excludes Savings Plans/RIs and services 'that would rapidly consume the entire AWS Free Tier credit amount', and the account is closed (data kept 90 days) unless upgraded. Free-tier-eligible EC2 types for these accounts are t3.micro/small, t4g.micro/small, c7i-flex.large, m7i-flex.large (whether other types are blocked on the Free plan is not stated verbatim on the pages checked). On the Paid plan the credits cover any EC2 usage. The legacy 750 h/month t2/t3.micro free tier only applies to accounts created before 2025-07-15.

Cheaper 4 vCPU/8 GiB options the card does not model (us-east-1 Linux on-demand, Price List 20260925174521): c6g.xlarge (Graviton2) $0.136, t3a.xlarge (4/16, burstable) $0.1504, c6a.xlarge (AMD Milan) $0.153, c5a.xlarge $0.154, c8g.xlarge (Graviton4) $0.15952, c7i-flex.xlarge $0.16958 (Flex: full performance 'a majority of the time'), c6i.xlarge $0.17 vs modelled c7i.xlarge $0.1785 / c7g.xlarge $0.145. Newer c8i.xlarge $0.18742, c7a.xlarge $0.20528 are dearer.

Cheapest Asia x86 region is Asia Pacific (Malaysia) ap-southeast-5 / (Thailand) ap-southeast-7: c7i.xlarge $0.17494 (-2% vs ap-south-1 $0.1785, ladder linear); ap-south-1 stays cheapest for m7i ($0.2121 vs $0.2142) and Graviton ($0.0982 vs $0.1416). EU: eu-north-1 confirmed cheapest of all 8 EU regions for c7i/m7i/c7g/m7g (eu-west-1 $0.19152, eu-south-2 $0.1915 c7i.xlarge).
macOS is not in this card (see aws-ec2-mac): Mac instances run only on Dedicated Hosts with a 24-hour minimum allocation.

T3/T4g launch in Unlimited mode by default (also for Spot), so the t3 surplus-credit charge applies unless the user switches to standard mode; new T8i burstable family surplus credits are $0.06/vCPU-h Linux, $0.115 Windows.

fleet.verification: Personal details, email and phone; payment card may be required.
fleet.tiers: EC2 grows On-Demand quotas with usage; requests via Service Quotas are also available.
fleet.notes: Published regional Standard-family vCPU baseline; applied quotas may differ for new accounts. G/VT and P GPU-family vCPU quotas start at zero. Windows shares EC2 quotas. Not an instance-count limit; capacity and IP quotas also constrain a fleet.
